profile.headline: Staff Platform Engineer | Distributed Systems & Workflow Orchestration | Building infrastructure for options, not optimizations
profile.summary:
I'm a Staff Platform Engineer who's spent 10+ years building the foundational systems that make complex distributed operations possible — and the last 5 years learning (sometimes the hard way) what you should build first.

At HashiCorp, I designed the infrastructure scaling strategy that took HCP from zero multi-environment capability to 65+ production clusters. The key insight wasn't a specific tool — it was that composable building blocks with clear ordering beat monolithic configurations every time, no matter how clever the abstraction.

My current focus is on what I call Infrastructure-as-Data: lifting orchestration above GitOps through API-driven contracts that let deployment tooling consume configuration programmatically instead of manipulating flat files across 85 isolated clusters. It's a hard sell internally (it always is), but the pattern is right.

What I'm exploring next:
→ How workflow orchestration patterns apply to agentic AI infrastructure
→ Auth and authorization models for AI agents (my L7 proxy + JWT work maps directly)
→ The intersection of platform engineering and the emerging AI toolchain

I got into infrastructure by accident — I was a frontend developer who got curious about why a Selenium box was unmanaged, and never looked back. That curiosity-first approach still drives everything I build.

If you're working on platform infrastructure, workflow orchestration, or the infrastructure layer for AI agents, I'd love to talk.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer | Hashicorp (IBM)
positions.description:
Driving technical strategy to unify infrastructure platforms across HashiCorp Cloud Platform and Terraform Cloud. Designing API-driven contracts and Infrastructure-as-Data patterns to replace flat-file configuration sprawl across 85 isolated clusters.

Key focus areas:
- Championing shared workflow orchestration platform across HCP and TFC, unifying existing Temporal-based systems with proven workspace pipeline patterns
- Authored RFC defining API consumption patterns for centralized configuration, pushing the platform from static file manipulation toward programmable infrastructure data
- Designed L7 authorization proxy with JWT integration for seamless browser/CLI authentication — a pattern directly applicable to agent-based auth models
- Stepped into interim team leadership during management transition, learning the distinction between technical vision and operational management firsthand
- HCP HashiStack pattern validated when TFC adopted it for self-managed Consul after HCP Consul sunset, scaling total environments to 65+ clusters

positions.title: Senior Engineer II — HashiCorp
positions.description:
Scaled the HCP infrastructure platform from proof-of-concept to production at enterprise scale.

- Evolved isolated HashiStack provisioning into ordered workspace pipeline with E2E standup — complete environments (Vault, Consul, Nomad, clients, cluster seeding, networking) in under 45 minutes, down from weeks of manual coordination
- Pattern adopted by 3 product data planes: Boundary, Vault Radar (acquisition onboarding), and Infragraph (net-new product)
- Reduced HashiStack disaster recovery from 6+ hours to under 30 minutes, enabling multi-region expansion (us-west-2, EU dual-region)
- Expanded cluster health canary into E2E integration test (Vault writes, Consul reads, Nomad job scheduling)
- Prototyped Vault lifecycle operator extension, establishing approach colleague drove to production

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer — HashiCorp
positions.description:
Proved that automated multi-environment provisioning was possible when no path existed, and built the architectural foundation the platform still scales on today.

- Won the architectural argument for isolated HashiStack environments over extending shared Nomad clients — authored technical case proving single-scheduler failure modes. Built first product data plane (Boundary), reaching Beta June 2022.
- Developed Module Composition philosophy — refactored all root modules into composable, testable building blocks that enabled ordered workspace orchestration
- Co-created distributed lifecycle operator for ASG management when CloudFormation couldn't handle Nomad client draining or raft leader awareness. Drove expansion to Consul raft management, pioneering testcontainers-based cluster state validation.
- Established service standup patterns defining how products deploy on HCP infrastructure — remain one of few engineers who understand the full infrastructure-to-service intersection

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer — Teem / WeWork
positions.description:
Core member of 2-person infrastructure team (growing to 4), building and operating all production AWS infrastructure for a growing SaaS platform.

- Sole implementer of 2ndQuadrant database architecture recommendations — managed VM-based PostgreSQL with ~200GB daily write volume, EC2 disk striping for IOPS, WAL management, and replica recovery
- Technical liaison for SOC-II compliance — vetted controls, bridged gap between off-the-shelf policy frameworks and engineering reality, helped drive audit completion in 6 months
- Built Grafana/InfluxDB monitoring. Hacked Okta SSO onto Elasticsearch/Kibana by forking official Docker build and injecting middleware into Hapi server
- Stood up Apache Airflow for data science team, enabling migration from ad-hoc notebooks to structured ETL pipelines
- Pioneered deployment patterns using custom Salt scripting for Django application lifecycle
